name: Binaural and isochronic tone layers under music (audio construction only)
goal: Build binaural (L/R frequency difference) and isochronic (gated carrier) layers under music: carrier pitch in key, beat/pulse rate, raised-cosine gating, pad foundation, notching the bed at the carrier, fades. No health claims.

sources.title: Producing a Binaural Beats Meditation Track in Ableton Live (Step-By-Step)
How to Create Isochronic Tones in Ableton Live with Huon Studio
Binaural Beats Are Boring… So I Built Something Else | Bisochronic® Studio
How to Create Monaural Beats in Ableton Live (Step-By-Step Tutorial)

theory: Binaural beat = |fL - fR| perceived on headphones only; isochronic = amplitude gating at the target rate audible on speakers. Raised-cosine edges (~3.75 ms) avoid clicks.
prerequisites: An existing music track to sit under

DAW (the presenter uses one) or a dedicated generator, or Web Audio: carrier OscillatorNodes per ear via ChannelMergerNode, right-ear frequency = carrier + beat(t); pulse gains from one master rate × ratio; StereoPannerNode for ping-pong (pan = sign of the pulse LFO); BiquadFilter lowpass with a slow LFO on the harmonic bus; noise buffer + slow auto-pan; beat(t) from setValueAtTime/linearRampToValueAtTime segments (implementation note)

DAW with a tone/isochronic generator or any synth + tremolo/LFO amplitude device, gain utility with automation, and a tuner, or Web Audio: OscillatorNode (sine) → GainNode; gain driven by a smoothed square/raised-cosine LFO whose frequency AudioParam is automated with linearRampToValueAtTime (implementation note)

DAW with stock pad/piano/bass instruments, reverb, echo/delay, EQ, utility gain and limiter, or Web Audio: two OscillatorNodes (f and f-Δ) each through a StereoPannerNode at -1/+1, a BiquadFilter type 'notch' at f with high Q on the music bus, a DynamicsCompressor as gentle limiter (implementation note)
Headphones for checking the binaural layer

outputs.name: result
outputs.description: Rendered part or recipe following the workflow

constraints: Portable recipe; not affiliated with any vendor; do not copy factory presets or sample packs.
Numbers in variants come from the source video transcripts; workflow steps are the consolidated mainstream practice.
Bring drums in early and avoid pitch wobble unless asked (user preferences from daily tests).

steps.action: Choose carrier in the song key (e.g. C5 523.25 Hz) and rate (e.g. 10 Hz, 14-18 Hz beta, 40 Hz).
Binaural: left = carrier, right = carrier + rate; layer octaves if desired.
Isochronic: gate a sine carrier at the rate with raised-cosine edges; verify rate in 20 s windows.
Music bed: slow pad, long reverb, ping-pong echo; notch the bed at the carrier pitch so the pulse stays clear.
Fade the layer in/out over 10-30 s; keep it 10-20 dB below the music.
Do not make health or cognitive claims in titles or text.
Hear the theory: run `/home/box/audio-tools/bin/python sample-lab/theory/entrainment_tones.py` from the repo root and compare the sections; reuse its functions as a starting point for renders.
steps.expect: WAV in sample-lab/theory/out/ demonstrating the principle

verification: Render a short test and A/B against a reference at matched loudness
Run the generator and confirm it writes a WAV without error
Check mono compatibility and that no element masks the kick/bass

variants.name: Produce a binaural-beat meditation track: a two-chord pad foundation with long reverb and overlapping glided notes, a sparse echoing piano and subtle bass, volume-automated arrangement, then a binaural layer of two pure sines (440 Hz and 432 Hz for an 8 Hz difference) panned hard left/right, a narrow high-Q EQ cut at the carrier frequency on the music bus so nothing masks it, fades, a gentle limiter (~3 dB input, no audible gain reduction) and WAV/MP3 export at 44.1 kHz
variants.goal: Make the whole track, not just the beat. Start from pads: play a simple two-chord loop (around A and D), add reverb with high decay and wet mix, keep chord changes on the grid, and let notes overlap with glide so transitions slide instead of stepping. Add a short piano line with an echo (more feedback, ping-pong on) and its own reverb, then a subtle low bass on the same roots; pull all levels down to avoid overdrive. Arrange by drawing volume automation so elements enter and leave (less is more; one element can carry minutes), boost the highs with a high shelf on bright parts, put delay before reverb. Binaural layer: a sine at the root frequency (A = 440 Hz) and a duplicate at 432 Hz (8 Hz difference); unpanned they make an audible wobble (monaural beat), panned hard left and right they form the binaural beat. Group the music and cut a narrow notch (high Q) at 440 Hz so the instrumental doesn't overlap the carrier. Fade the beat in and out, keep it quiet but present when muted/unmuted. On the master, add a limiter on the loudest section with only ~3 dB input and no audible gain reduction; export 44.1 kHz WAV plus an MP3, then do a calm test listen later and adjust.
steps: Pick a soft pad, play a simple two-chord loop (e.g. A then D), add reverb with high decay and wet mix, capture the MIDI and align chord changes to the grid; loop it.
Layer a second pad for texture and a sparse piano phrase; add an echo with more feedback and ping-pong, plus a reverb with moderated wet mix.
Lengthen notes so they overlap at chord changes and enable glide so pitch slides between them.
Add a subtle low bass on the roots; lower all instrument levels to avoid clipping.
Arrange with volume automation: bring elements in and out gradually; high-shelf boost and mid cut on bright parts; put delay before reverb.
Binaural layer: a sine instrument at 440 Hz and a duplicate at 432 Hz; listen unpanned (wobble), then pan one hard left and one hard right; program one note across the whole track.
Group the music tracks and add a narrow, high-Q EQ cut at 440 Hz on the group.
Fade the beat in and out; set its level so it is quiet but noticeably different when muted.
On the master, loop the loudest section and add a limiter with about 3 dB input and no audible gain reduction; export WAV 44.1 kHz and an MP3; test-listen later in a calm setting and adjust.

variants.name: Add an isochronic pulse layer under an existing track: a sine (or noise) carrier played by one long MIDI note, amplitude-pulsed at a chosen rate (e.g. 4 Hz) with a smooth-step pulse shape and a 0–100% isochronic blend, faded in and out by gain automation, with the pulse rate automated (e.g. 15 Hz → 4 Hz → 15 Hz) using ~10 ms parameter smoothing, carrier tuned by reference (440/432) or a custom note-to-frequency map and verified with a tuner, then mixed barely audible
variants.goal: Build the Mind Amend-style isochronic layer as its own track. A tone generator plays a sine carrier from MIDI; with beat frequency 0 it is just a plain sine. Pick the pulse rate (e.g. 4 Hz) and raise the isochronic blend from 0% (steady tone) through 50% to 100% (full on/off pulses); choose a smooth-step pulse shape for focused but soft pulses. An amplitude-pulsing (LFO/tremolo) device lets you pulse noise or any audio as well. Use one long MIDI note for an uninterrupted tone (chords also work and pulse together). Fade in over about 30 s and out over 30–60 s with gain automation. Automate the pulse rate with exact typed breakpoints (e.g. start 15 Hz, glide to 4 Hz, return to 15 Hz at the end) and set the device's parameter smoothing to its minimum (0.01 = 10 ms) for automation. Keep pulse rates low (the speaker suggests below ~100 Hz); carrier frequencies (e.g. 432 Hz reference tuning, or a custom mapping where a note equals 528 Hz) are a separate layer of choice; check the actual pitch with a tuner set to the same reference. Finally set the layer's level in the mixer so it sits barely audible under the music. Polyrhythm Studio: OscillatorNode → GainNode whose gain follows a pulse-shaped LFO at rate r(t) with a ramped automation curve.
steps: Create a MIDI track with the tone generator; set the device output low (about -20 dB) so the layer starts quiet.
Program one long MIDI note (or loop a short note while designing; chords also work).
Set the pulse rate (e.g. 4 Hz) and raise isochronic blend from 0% to 100%; choose a smooth-step pulse shape.
Add a gain utility and automate a ~30 s fade-in at the start and a 30–60 s fade-out at the end.

Expose the pulse-rate parameter for automation, set parameter smoothing to 0.01 (10 ms), and draw breakpoints with typed values: 15 Hz at the start, 4 Hz in the middle section, back to 15 Hz at the end.

Optional carrier tuning: switch the tuning reference (440 → 432 Hz) or load a custom note-to-frequency map and find the note that gives the target frequency (e.g. 528 Hz); confirm with a tuner set to the same reference.
Set the track fader so the layer is barely audible under the music.

variants.name: Layered binaural + isochronic track architecture: carrier in the left ear and carrier+beat in the right (e.g. 100/104 or 100/110 Hz), octave-up/down copies for depth, an isochronic pulse ratio-locked to the beat rate (1:1, 1:2, 2:1) with sine pulse shape, optional left-right ping-pong pulsing, extra harmonic/anchor tone layers pulsed at the same rate, a slow lowpass sweep that fades harmonic layers in and out, panned drifting pink/white/brown noise atmosphere, a drone a fifth below, and a 'journey' of timed beat-rate segments with smooth ramps (e.g. 10 → 1.5 Hz descent)
variants.goal: Design richer Mind Amend-style tracks than a bare two-tone beat. Binaural: one pure tone per ear, the right ear tone = carrier + beat (100 Hz left, 104 Hz right gives a 4 Hz beat; removing one ear leaves a steady tone). Isochronic: the same rate as on/off pulsing of a tone; both can play together. Choose any comfortable carrier (100 Hz in the demo, with micro-tuning), add octave layers (½× and 2× carrier) for depth, and pulse layers at a rate locked to the beat by a simple ratio (1:1, half, double) so nothing drifts out of sync when the beat changes; sine pulse shape is preferred. Ping-pong pulse alternates the pulse left/right instead of on/off. Extra harmonic tones (the presenter uses solfeggio-labelled frequencies and says they lack scientific basis) or a fifth/12th harmonic stack are pulsed at the same rate. A lowpass sweep (period ~6 s and longer) fades harmonic layers in and out so no tone is constant. Pink/white/brown noise as wind/ocean air, auto-panned. A low drone a fifth below supports the field. A journey timeline holds a beat rate for set minutes, then glides smoothly to the next (5 Hz 5 min → 2 Hz → 1 Hz; sleep descent 10 → 1.5 Hz; a 12 → 4.5 Hz ramp). Polyrhythm Studio: one shared rate LFO drives beat offset and every pulse lane via integer ratios.
steps: Set the carrier (e.g. 100 Hz pure sine) in the left ear and carrier + beat in the right (e.g. 104 Hz for 4 Hz). Check with headphones: removing one side leaves a steady tone.
Add octave copies at half and double the carrier at lower level.
Add an isochronic pulse with sine shape on a layer at ratio 1:1 to the beat; try half and double. Change the beat and confirm the pulse follows.
Optional ping-pong: pulse the layer left/right instead of on/off and raise depth.
Add harmonic/anchor tones (e.g. a fifth or 12th above, or chosen fixed tones) pulsed at the same rate or left steady.
Put a slow lowpass sweep on the harmonic layers (start ~6 s period, then longer) with adjustable intensity.
Add a low pink/white/brown noise layer with slow auto-pan, and a low drone a fifth below.
Build a journey: hold each beat rate for set minutes and glide to the next (e.g. 5 Hz 5 min → 2 Hz 5 min → 1 Hz; or a 10 → 1.5 Hz descent); export and keep a card listing every frequency and ratio.

variants.name: Speaker-safe brainwave layer in a DAW: either two fixed-frequency sines a few Hz apart summed in mono (e.g. carrier + 8 Hz for alpha), or a tremolo (auto-pan set to tremolo, high amount, ~40% shape) at the entrainment rate on a playable pad so chords themselves pulse, optionally with the sine pair underneath
variants.goal: Build a monaural beat that works on speakers as well as headphones, and turn ordinary pads into the entrainment source. Delta vs brainwave cluster (isochronic layer as its own track, binaural per-ear tones): this one puts a tremolo at the target rate directly on a playable pad/chord track and uses an in-mono two-sine pair instead of per-ear panning.
steps: Option A: load a sine synth, set the oscillator to fixed frequency at the carrier (a key note).
Put it in a rack/group, duplicate the chain, and set the second sine to carrier + target rate (e.g. +8 Hz). Keep both centred (mono).
Check: mute one chain and the wobble disappears; both together give the monaural beat.
Option B: on a pad or chord track, add a tremolo (auto-pan in tremolo mode), raise the amount high, set shape ~40%, and set the rate to the target Hz (e.g. 8 Hz).
Turn off fixed pitch so the instrument plays normally; play chords and melodies so the whole harmony pulses.
Add reverb after the tremolo and, if wanted, keep the Option A sine pair quietly underneath.
Optionally copy the same tremolo onto other tracks of a meditation piece, then test-listen at length before sharing.
